System Map

Read together, the five themes are not separate pressures. Four loops connect them: an experience drought in which AI takes over junior tasks and the pool of experienced staff thins, a frozen market in which fewer leavers mean fewer openings, a bargaining brake in which concern about AI produces agreements that set conditions on its use, and a flattening loop in which agents and management cuts feed each other. Arrows that cross a colour are connections no single theme carries.

Swipe sideways to see the whole map.

LoopNameWhat it doesThis cycle
R1Experience drought
First jobs		AI takes over junior tasks, fewer juniors are hired, fewer people learn on the job, and a thinner experienced pool pushes firms to lean harder on AI.Turning: 19% gap for under-25s
R2Frozen market
Careers and training		Fewer people leave, so fewer vacancies open, so fewer people can move.Turning: quits at 1.9%
B1Bargaining brake
Rules for AI at work		More AI at work raises concern, concern produces agreements, and agreements set conditions on how AI is used.Priming: 108 agreements
R3Flattening loop
Agents and managers		Agents let firms cut management layers, and fewer managers push more work to agents.Priming: 41% report layers cut

Hover over a status for its meaning: Turning means every step in the loop has current evidence, so it is running now; Priming means the parts are in place but the circle has not yet closed at scale.

The Scenario Matrix’s horizontal axis asks how strongly B1 Bargaining brake works, that is whether AI terms are agreed with workers or set by employers alone; its vertical axis asks whether R2 Frozen market keeps careers inside organisations or the open market moves again.

What it means: The two reinforcing loops on the left, the experience drought and the frozen market, both run through the pool of experienced staff, so an employer that cuts junior intake and training at the same time is pulling on the same thread twice. The levers an employer controls are how junior roles are designed, whether training leads to internal moves, whether AI terms are agreed, and who owns each agent.
